note: The walker's pack of cloth pouches and the piles at camp (docs/future/13 sections 4.1 and 4.5). startPouches: pouches from the start; perCarrier: pouches each made carrier adds (satchel, basket, frame), so 6, 8, 10, 12; handfulsPerPouch: Gather taps that fill one pouch (one look step each). groups: the fixed sort order of pouches, never shown. partGroups: the group of a plant-part kind '<species>.<part>' that kinds does not list. kinds: one row per non-plant kind, in sort order within its group; sketch names its drawing, camp is the camp slot its pile prefers ('sticks', 'stones', 'clay', 'heap' for the first free heap slot), or where it goes instead ('rack' for herbs, 'bowl' for food, 'none' for worms, which dig themselves in, 'pouch' for seeds and clumps, which wait for a hole); a pile whose preferred slot is taken by another kind falls back to the first free heap slot. name: the pouch card's title; line: the card's one line. piles: handfuls a ground pile holds, the top of each look step (small, good, big), the rack's bunches and the handfuls a rack bunch or bowl holds. piles.look (src/world/pack/draw.js, piles.js pileShape): models, the model each kind's pile wears ('stick', 'stick-pale' the same paler, 'stone'; a kind not listed wears otherModel); models3d, the camp model files (meters, base on the ground, front +z), coloured from their base colour map; footprintM, each model's width across; stageShares, the share of a model's pieces shown at each look step (small, good, big heap, then the full pile, all its handfuls): a pile builds up piece by piece from the bottom at its real size, never scaled (Matt, October 22, 2026); heapShare, the bottom pieces a K-21 heap shows. stack: the stick pile built from one log (Matt's single log, model; a round stand-in of radiusM, lenM, bark and end until it loads), its rows from the bottom, each log resting in the groove of the two below; sizeJitter, gapM, slideM, yawJitterDeg and tintJitter seed each copy, shades the tints it is drawn in; the stages show stageShares of its logs, a heap heapShare; logMax, the most logs and stones drawn near you. stones: the stone pile built from one stone (Matt's single stone, model; a lumpy stand-in of halfWM, halfHM and color until it loads): count stones set down one at a time, each where it rests lowest among tries seeded places within radiusM (on the ground or nestled on stones already there), with sizeJitter, tintJitter and shades as the logs'. A model fused into one surface, its largest piece holding more than mostPieceShare of it (the scanned camp piles, October 22, 2026), cannot build up that way: it is drawn whole at fusedScales of its size per step and fusedHeapScale for a heap, until it comes with separate pieces; yawJitterDeg, a pile's seeded turn from its slot's; sinkM, how far it sits into the ground; pale, drift twigs' colour mixed toward a grey; standIn, the seeded mound of crossed sticks and cairn of stones drawn until the models load (rings: count, ring radius share, height share); pass, the contact shadow's length (m at scale 1) and darkness; nearM, max, drawn within this far of you, at most this many; rebuildS, moveM, refreshS: the lists are rebuilt at most every rebuildS, at once on a change, after moving moveM, and every refreshS anyway. pickups: what lies on the ground at a gather spot with something left today (pickup-meshes.js), drawn scale times their real size so they can be found (as creatures are; their real sizes are below), within nearM, at most max shapes (nearest spots first), variants seeded shapes a kind; per kind, count is [least, most] shapes when full (fewer as it is picked over), lenM, radiusM and bend a stick's, sizeM, heightShare, lump and sink a stone's, color its linear albedo, spreadM how far round the spot they scatter. heaps: K-21 heaps left when the pack is full; cap is how many lie out at once, tapM their tap radius. pot: water classes the clay pot fills from, and whether it takes sea water. rill: when the hint about a rill to camp shows. ui: pouch tap target, gap and drawing size in px (Matt, October 22, 2026: 48 px targets). words: every line the pack, piles and pot say.
carriersNote: P2f (Matt, October 26, 2026): carriers replace, never stack. The walker wears one at a time: the starting pack (startPouches), or a made carrier in carriers' order, each perCarrier pouches more than the one before (the satchel 8, the basket 10, the frame 12, Phase 3). A carrier is made at the workbench (cook.json makes, out 'carrier') and put on at once; the one taken off hangs at camp, and its card's Wear swaps back, if what the pack holds fits its pouches. wear: how each made carrier sits on the figure (src/world/camp/carriers.js): model, the camp model it wears (camp.json props.models); bone, the figure bone that carries it (the satchel at the hip, the basket on the pack bone's spring); at, its model's origin (base middle) in rest model meters; turnDeg, pitch, yaw and roll of the model before the bone turns it; scale, of its real size. Wearing one hides the baked pack (the figure's pack region). hang: where the carriers not worn hang at camp, by the workbench (slot), spots in the bench's own frame (x across, y up, z toward where you work, m), one per carrier in order (the starting pack first), each with its yaw (deg) and a click radius r.

satchel.note: October 29, 2026 (Matt): low behind on the pack bone, clear of the arms (it rode the hip at one side and the arm swung through it); its straps are painted on the coat (figure.json straps).

kinds.name: Sticks
kinds.line: Dry sticks from under the bushes.

kinds.name: Drift twigs
kinds.line: Salt-grey twigs from the tide line.

kinds.name: Reed down
kinds.line: Soft reed down for tinder.

kinds.name: Reed leaves
kinds.line: Long reed leaves, split and twisted for cord.

kinds.name: King Alfred's cakes
kinds.line: Black knobs from an old log. They hold a spark.

kinds.name: Charcoal
kinds.line: Charcoal from the fire's edge. It draws.

kinds.name: Pebbles
kinds.line: Round stones from the shore.

kinds.name: Flat stones
kinds.line: Flat stones that split along their grain.

kinds.name: Rushes
kinds.line: Tough green rush stems, for twisting into cord.

kinds.name: Marram leaves
kinds.line: Grey-green marram leaves, rolled tight and strong.

kinds.name: Rush cord
kinds.line: Two-ply cord, twisted by hand.

kinds.name: Willow withies
kinds.line: Long bendy willow shoots, cut in late winter.

kinds.name: Gorse flowers
kinds.line: Yellow pea flowers that smell of coconut.

kinds.name: Willow bark
kinds.line: Strips of grey willow bark.

kinds.name: Lichen twigs
kinds.line: Twigs grey with lichen, blown down in the wind.

kinds.name: Water mint
kinds.line: Water mint leaves. They smell of mint when crushed.

kinds.name: Meadowsweet
kinds.line: Frothy meadowsweet flowers, sweet as honey.

kinds.name: Nettle tops
kinds.line: Young nettle tops, picked with care.

kinds.name: Chamomile
kinds.line: Chamomile flowers. They smell of apples.

kinds.name: Lily leaf
kinds.line: A broad lily leaf, cool and waxy, picked from the pond.

kinds.name: Pondweed
kinds.line: A dripping handful of curled pondweed, pulled from the pond.

kinds.name: Sand
kinds.line: Dry sand from above the tide.

kinds.name: Clay
kinds.line: Blue-grey clay, cool and sticky.

kinds.name: Wood ash
kinds.line: Soft grey ash from the cold ring.

kinds.name: Crushed shell
kinds.line: Shell ground to grit in the mortar.

kinds.name: Eggs
kinds.line: A brown egg from the hen. Never for the creatures.

kinds.name: Eggshells
kinds.line: The shells from a breakfast. Ground in the mortar, they make grit for the hen.

kinds.name: Eggshell grit
kinds.line: Eggshell ground fine in the mortar. Laying hens need it.

kinds.name: Sea salt
kinds.line: Salt the sun left in a stone pan above the tide. A pinch at a time, and never for the creatures.

kinds.name: Fallen leaves
kinds.line: Fallen leaves, dry and brown.

kinds.name: Cast kelp
kinds.line: Long kelp the spring tide cast up.

kinds.name: Wrack
kinds.line: Wrack from the strandline.

kinds.name: Broken shells
kinds.line: Broken shells from the strandline, bleached by the sun.

kinds.name: Worms
kinds.line: Worms in a little damp soil.

kinds.name: Acorns
kinds.line: Acorns from under the oak.

kinds.name: Hazelnuts
kinds.line: Hazelnuts in their green frills.

kinds.name: Old comb
kinds.line: Old comb a wild colony left behind.

kinds.name: Chanterelle
kinds.line: Golden chanterelles that smell of apricot.

kinds.name: Charcoal sticks
kinds.line: Thin sticks of willow charcoal, for drawing. They wear down as you sketch.

kinds.name: Clay bowls
kinds.line: Fired clay bowls, nested one in another. A handful is one bowl.

kinds.name: Leaf pack
kinds.line: Fallen leaves bound with rush cord, to sink in still water.

kinds.name: Lily leaf parcel
kinds.line: Worms wrapped in a lily leaf and tied with rush cord, for the turtles.

kinds.name: Woven twigs
kinds.line: Drift twigs woven into one springy length, for a shovel's haft.

kinds.name: Lantern pot
kinds.line: A fired clay housing, pierced all round. It wants a post and a rush wick.

kinds.name: Lantern
kinds.line: A clay lantern on a short post. Set it down where you want a light at night.

kinds.name: Deep clay
kinds.line: Dark, dense clay from a spade below the blue-grey. It stands up to heat.

kinds.name: Iron ore
kinds.line: Black sand from the spring pool, heavy in the hand. It clings to a knife's iron.

kinds.name: Copper ore
kinds.line: Small pebbles flecked with green, washed out of the spring pool.

kinds.name: Iron
kinds.line: A dull grey bloom of iron from the furnace, hammered into a lump.

kinds.name: Copper
kinds.line: A small red-brown lump of copper from the furnace. It never rusts in the sea.

kinds.name: Nails
kinds.line: A handful of square nails, drawn out at the furnace.

kinds.name: Twisted sticks
kinds.line: Two sticks twisted round each other and bound, stiff and straight.

kinds.name: Planks
kinds.line: A short plank of twisted sticks nailed across. Kept for the dock.

heap.note: October 29, 2026 (Matt: clay and everything set down showed as wood): a kind models does not list is a soft mound in its own colour (colors, else its pickup colour, else its group's), with a few of its own pickup pieces on top when it has a pickup shape. radiiM: the full pile's mound half-widths and height; stageScales: its size at the small, good and big heap and the full pile; heapScale: a K-21 heap's; lump, sink: as a pebble's; pieces: pickup pieces on top of a full pile.

pale.note: Drift twigs on the stick pile, mixed this much toward salt-grey (0.45 until October 29, 2026: at log size it read as grey wood, Matt).

pickups.treatNote: P2h: a treat set out and lying is drawn as a small heap of its kind's pickups within treatSpreadM of where it was set, treatScale times their size (drawn first, so the strandline's own never crowd it out); one set in water lies treatSink.startM under the surface and sinks perH meters a game hour until it rests on the bed; over its last hours (treats.json paleH) it is drawn mixed treatPale.mix toward the ground's colour and lower, then it is gone.

stores.note: The stores (docs/future/13 section 3.12, Matt, October 23, 2026): places at the camp's sticks, stones and clay slots, drawn empty and waiting from the first frame (src/world/pack/stores.js, draw.js). Each has a card even when empty: name, then the pile's kind and word, or empty. r: how far from the slot's middle a click finds it; glowM: its soft glow's radius while the pack holds its kind near camp. sticks.look: the wood store, two forked stakes stakeZM either side of the row (driven sinkM in, forked at forkM, tines tineM long opening tineDeg), a crossbar barR thick resting in the forks and barOverM past them, and flat stones (stones: their middles, stoneR radii) the logs lie on, floorLiftM high. stones.look: a shallow scrape radiusM across (floorM, rimM: its floor's and rim's height) ringed by edging stones of the pile's own stone, edgeSize times its size, edgeAtM from the middle. clay.look: one flat stone, radii and colour (linear).

store.note: The camp store (docs/future/13 P2j; src/world/pack/store.js): a lidded rush hamper with slots[0] slots, slots[1] once a second hamper stacks on it; one kind a slot, up to handfuls a slot (a pile's worth). Its card shows the slots as drawn icons with the pile words, never a number; Take up on a slot fills one pouch. Set down at camp goes to a kind's own place first (the rack, the wood store, the stone pile, the clay slab), then the hamper (src/world/pack/route.js). Once a hamper stands, the heap slots retire and what they held moves in. look: the hamper made in code (vertex colours; colour where it has none), then the stacked pair, drawn with the stores facing the fire (src/world/pack/draw.js).

words.emptied: You tip it out. The island takes it back.
words.heap: A small heap you left here.
words.pileFull: This heap is as big as it gets.
words.noSlot: The camp has all it needs. Set something aside first.
words.noRack: Herbs want somewhere to hang. A drying rack would hold them.
words.rackFull: The rack is full. Take a bunch down first.
words.hamperFull: The hamper is full. Take something out first.
words.noBowl: This wants a bowl to sit in.
words.worms: They wriggle down into the soil.
words.clump: Its roots are bare. Set it in the ground to keep it.
words.pouch: Seed and clumps keep in their pouch, or in a hamper once there is one.

carrierLines.pack: Six cloth pouches on a strap. It hangs here while you wear another.
carrierLines.satchel: Plaited rushes on a cord strap. Eight pouches.
carrierLines.basket: Woven withies on two cord straps. Ten pouches.

words.worn: You hang the other up by the bench.
words.wearFull: The pack holds more than this one has pouches. Set something down first.

pot.still: This water stands still. The spring runs cleaner.
pot.away: The pot belongs by the fire.
pot.arms: Your arms are full with the pot.

words.rillHint: Water could come down to the camp by itself, if it had a way.
words.rillNote: The spring's water runs past the camp now. No more carrying.
